messages:
Liam: Hey team — got hit with a $180 charge for allergy injections yesterday. Provider says they billed CPT 95165 (immunotherapy) but carrier denied saying the service was non-covered for adults under our preventive rider. I paid at checkout. I have the itemized receipt, the EOB showing denial reason, and the provider claim stub. Can benefits help get this reimbursed or reprocessed?

Alex (People Ops): Sorry that happened, Liam. Yes — we can help escalate. Two parallel routes: 1) We can request a claim re-adjudication from the carrier if the procedure should be covered (we'll need the itemized bill + EOB + a short note from the provider confirming CPT and medical necessity). 2) If the provider miscoded, ask them to submit a corrected claim with the proper CPT/modifier. Either way upload docs and we'll file on your behalf.

Liam: Is there a quick checklist of exactly what you need so I can get it uploaded? Provider billing office asked if I wanted them to submit anything directly.

Marta (Benefits): Checklist: (a) Itemized receipt showing date of service and amount paid; (b) Carrier EOB/denial PDF; (c) Provider claim stub (CMS-1500 or electronic claim print); (d) Short provider note on letterhead stating medical necessity for immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis (if available). If provider will submit corrected claim themselves, request they use the original claim number and mark it "Corrected/Reprocessed - subscriber payment".

Alex (People Ops): Timeline: once we have complete docs we submit to the carrier and typical re-adjudication is 7-14 business days. If provider will resubmit corrected claim, processing can be similar but sometimes faster. If the provider refuses to correct, we can request a provider appeal on your behalf.

Liam: Can I get an advance reimbursement from Redwood until the carrier sorts it? I paid out of pocket and it's a bit tight this week.

Marta (Benefits): We do not offer cash advances for medical claims. Two options: 1) We can prioritize the appeal with an "EXPEDITE" flag if you have a collections due date; 2) We can draft a provider hold letter so collections are paused while the appeal is open. If it's urgent, upload the bill and include any collections notice and mark the upload subject as "URGENT - collections".

BenefitsBot: Upload portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/upload (choose "Medical - Claim Reprocessing"). Provider hold letter template: https://benefits.redwood.com/templates/provider-hold-letter.pdf. For secure docs use: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload.

Liam: Uploading itemized receipt + EOB now. I'll also ask the clinic to send a brief medical necessity note and to resubmit the corrected claim with original claim number. Thanks for the quick help! :thumbsup:
